summary: Verified admin/user session ISOLATION in the same browser. All critical isolation invariants hold: admin login does NOT wipe the user's ni_token/ni_user; admin logout preserves user session; user logout preserves admin session. Regular user can reach /dashboard, admin can reach /pentest/fuser, and both coexist simultaneously in localStorage. Production redeploy will fix the reported bug.

test_scenarios_executed.scenario: Admin login at /pentest/fuser/login (same browser context) -> /pentest/fuser console loads with data
test_scenarios_executed.storage_after: localStorage: ni_token + ni_user + ni_admin_token + ni_admin_user (ALL FOUR PRESENT)

test_scenarios_executed.scenario: CRITICAL — user session preserved after admin login (same browser)
test_scenarios_executed.evidence: ni_token & ni_user unchanged after admin login; /dashboard still authenticated (no redirect to /login)

test_scenarios_executed.scenario: Admin console still authenticated after visiting /dashboard and returning
REVERSE 1 — Admin Logout at /pentest/fuser preserves user session
test_scenarios_executed.evidence: After clicking 'Logout' in admin console: ni_admin_token/ni_admin_user cleared; ni_token/ni_user intact; /dashboard still loads as user

test_scenarios_executed.scenario: REVERSE 2 — User Logout at /dashboard preserves admin session
test_scenarios_executed.evidence: After clicking sidebar 'Sign out' on /dashboard (data-testid=logout-btn): ni_token/ni_user cleared; ni_admin_token/ni_admin_user intact; redirects to /login. Note: first attempt was blocked by welcome-aboard modal; after dismissing modal, logout works and admin session is preserved.

ui_bugs.issue: First-time-user welcome modal overlays the sidebar and blocks clicks on 'Sign out' (and any sidebar nav) until dismissed. Users may perceive Sign out as broken on first load. Modal appears to have no visible close/dismiss button on this desktop viewport (only 'Get started' CTA).

critical_code_review_comments: The problem statement references admin login at /admin/login, but the actual route is /pentest/fuser/login (see /app/frontend/src/App.js:63). /admin/login falls through to the catch-all Navigate to /login. Confirm docs/reports use the correct path.

AuthContext.setSession + logout + api.js pickTokenForUrl and 401 interceptor correctly implement per-slot session isolation. The three-slot design (ni_admin_token, sessionStorage ni_token for impersonation, localStorage ni_token for user) is sound and verified end-to-end.
api.js interceptor 401 handler is scoped: /admin/* 401 clears only admin slot; other 401 clears only user slot. Verified logic-wise; not exercised in this run.

Minor: AuthContext.jsx monkey-patches window.history.pushState (line 103-108) to detect route changes. This global side effect can conflict with other libraries; consider using react-router's useLocation() hook to re-run hydrateUser on route change instead.

Minor: hydrateUser() falls back across scopes (admin -> session -> local, or user -> session -> local -> admin). This is convenient but means the displayed user in headers can silently switch scope. Verified behavior is intentional per comments in file.
action_items: Redeploy production — codebase already contains the correct token-separation refactor; the reported bug ('logging into admin logs out user') is NOT reproducible in the current preview build.
(Optional) Add a close (X) button to the first-time welcome-aboard modal on /dashboard so users can dismiss it without clicking the primary CTA.

rca of the issue: Production is running an older build that used a single ni_token slot for both admin and regular user sessions, causing the second login (in either direction) to overwrite the first. The current preview codebase (/app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx + /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js) already implements three independent slots (ni_admin_token, sessionStorage ni_token for impersonation, localStorage ni_token for user) and scope-aware setSession/logout/interceptor logic. Verified end-to-end: after user login + admin login in the same browser, ALL FOUR localStorage keys coexist and both sessions remain authenticated. Mitigation: deploy the current preview build to production.
